query: Automotive injection molding machinery import tariffs

statements.text: This exemption expired at the start of 2020, meaning 25% tariffs on injection molds made in China are a reality once more.

Annex III of the proclamation provides temporary relief for certain plastics machinery, parts, and molds, including specified Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) lines 8477 and 8480. For these products, a combined duty cap of 15% will apply through Dec. 31, 2027.

The immediate impact of this tariff was short-lived, however, as of December in the same year, Chinese tooling imports were granted a one-year exemption, in part as a result of concern that the tariff would severely disrupt manufacturing supply chains and damage bottom lines.
Since 2018, the U.S. has implemented a series of Section 301 tariffs, many of which target goods from China, including injection molds and molded plastic parts.

The administration has announced a 15% tariff on specific metal-insensitive industrial and electrical grid equipment and a 10% levy on imported goods made entirely of steel, aluminum, or copper from the US, effective through 2027.

Bottom line: We can expect cost increases throughout the supply chain as a result of the 25% tariff on Chinese imports, and the sourcing of tooling in custom plastic injection molding is likely to be hit hard.
Starting Jan. 1, 2028, Annex III products will transition to standard tariff treatment outlined in the proclamation.
These tariffs range from 10% to 25% and add significantly to the cost of importing tools and components from overseas.
A mold that once cost $20,000 from China could now cost $25,000 or more after tariffs.

On July 6, 2018, the U.S. government instituted a 25% tariff on Chinese imports (including tooling used in custom injection molding), igniting concerns among domestic mold builders and manufacturers who had relied on Chinese imports for tooling.
